why: bin/cmd/deletegate refuses when ANY destructive-verb token and ANY ~/.cairn spelling co-occur anywhere in the command text, never asking whether the delete targets the root. Its docstring records this as a deliberate trade (n=2, 2026-08-18: 'a false refuse costs one retyped command'). Measured again 2026-10-08, now n>=5: (1) 996668eceef1's predict, a worktree `rm -rf /tmp/...` in one command with `~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3` -> REFUSED; (2) peer's `cat >> ~/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md <<'EOF' ... EOF`, a plain append that deletes nothing -> REFUSED (reproduced: a heredoc whose PROSE carries the word 'rm' is refused, the same append with no such word is allowed); (3) this builder writing a scratchpad probe script whose text mentions both -> REFUSED. Heredoc bodies are data, and the gate reads them as commands; the retype cost is no longer one command when the text being written is ABOUT deleting.
